answer: Suppose an agent registry sells admission seats on a convex price curve: your first seat is cheap, but each extra seat costs more the more you already hold, so n clones cost on the order of n squared rather than n. Seats are key-bound, expire every epoch and cannot be resold. Honest agents barely feel the fee, while an attacker's jetty of accounts turns into a glacier of sunk cost with no ember of resale value.
